name: Construct Capital
identity_check: Confirmed as Construct Capital (constructcap.com; legal entity Construct Capital Management, LLC per the site's terms of use), the early-stage VC firm Dayna Grayson (ex-NEA) and Rachel Holt (ex-Uber) founded in 2020 to back founders rebuilding 'foundational industries' (manufacturing, logistics, mobility, critical infrastructure, defense, energy); also written 'Construct'. TechCrunch (Feb 2021) places the team in Washington, D.C.; its LinkedIn company page (linked from the site) matches the founders and description. Not a construction or construction-tech investor despite the name, and not dConstruct (the Singapore robotics company with its own round file in this repo).

thesis_text.value: Early-stage firm backing founders who bring software, automation, AI and connected hardware to long-neglected foundational industries: manufacturing, logistics, mobility, critical infrastructure, defense and energy. It argues these sectors carry much of GDP yet have seen little disruptive technology, and that tech-first, domestic reindustrialization is needed for American resilience and productivity.

open_items: No application form or apply URL: the site only offers a general 'sayhello@' contact email (not recorded). Cold inbound is inferred from 'Reach out if you're a founder transforming a foundational industry.'

Nothing found on investing in Indian founders or on requiring a US entity. The point-of-view page stresses domestic (US) industry, but the portfolio includes Toronto-based Polygrade and Latin American Vammo.

HQ comes from a 2021 TechCrunch mention of a D.C. lease; no current street address on constructcap.com (terms page gives only a Delaware governing-law clause). An unverified search hint placed the firm in Chevy Chase, Maryland. SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent, so Form D filings (fund legal names, addresses, exact sizes) were not checked.
The site's news list carries a Bloomberg headline (2026-09-18) that Construct 'reached $1 billion in assets'; the article is paywalled (403), so any new fund behind the jump from $750M is unknown.
Legal name of the $75M 2022 later-stage/'select' vehicle and exact final-close dates of Funds I-III not published; close dates are announcement dates.

Rounds not recorded because the round page was blocked (403) or does not name Construct: Torch (Axios), Nauta 2026 strategic raise (Axios Pro), Amca $76M launch (Axios Pro), EZ Health $26M (Axios Pro), Hadrian (CNBC), General Robotics (GeekWire). Vammo's earlier seed (Construct-led 'three years ago') and Construct's earlier Hadrian rounds were not re-checked.
Amounts not stated for Endurance Energy Series A; HQ/founding year not stated for several companies (Torch, Endurance, Shade, Sphere Semi, Nauta, Folio, Didero, ChargeLab).
Sphere Semi: the $20M combines a $12.5M round led by Acme and Future Ventures and $7.5M of formation capital led by Construct; recorded as one entry, stage undisclosed.

Partner focus_sectors are classified from the homepage bios (Grayson: NEA manufacturing/automation deals such as Desktop Metal, Onshape, Tulip, Formlabs; Holt: Uber Rides and New Mobility; Wan: The Engine deals such as Form Energy and Commonwealth Fusion; Saruhashi: fintech background but works with Nauta, Nexxa AI, Amplio, Advex; Chamlin: supply chain and manufacturing operator, Podium and BackOps). The firm does not assign sector coverage to partners.
